        The market research
        
A rising share of a
£6bn market

        
UK fire & safety market: ~£6bn today, projected £8.5bn by 2030. Drag the timeline to watch Freedom's share of it climb.

      

      
      

        
Overall ecommerce

        
All UK online retail of physical goods, £132bn in 2026 · drag to move through the years

        

          

            
            

            
ONS internet retail sales: about £132bn of physical products bought online in 2026, nearly 29% of all UK retail spending. Fire safety ecommerce (£380m) is around 0.3% of that, roughly £1 in every £347 spent online.

Fire & safety ecommerce

        
The slice of that market already bought online, £380m in 2026 · drag to move through the years

        

          

            
            

            
Management estimate: the £1.81bn equipment market at manufacturer prices, uplifted to end customer value, at a 16% online share. Grown 8% a year, ahead of the 5% market but below general retail.

0
average fire safety spend per UK business, every year

        
0
of fire safety per person over a lifetime, about £87 a year

        
0
if just 1% of the UK bought one £30 fire product

      

      
Put simply: the UK spends £6bn a year on fire safety. That works out at about £1,053 per business, or £87 per person every year — around £3,000 each over a lifetime. Most products cost about £30, so if just 1% of the UK bought one, that alone is £20.7m of sales. The market is huge because these are small, repeat purchases that the law requires.

How the mix shifts

          The conditions
          
What the £100 million ambition assumes

          
A long term value creation target, not a current valuation. Reaching it depends on all of the following holding true.

        

        

          
01Channel executionAmazon, Shopify, OnBuy and TikTok Shop all launch and scale on plan, alongside eBay and Temu.

          
02Working capitalStock funding keeps pace with demand, so availability and marketplace ranking are never the constraint.

          
03Brand portfolioThe owned brands repeat the Firestorm model across batteries, PPE, aerosols, cleaning and automotive.

          
04Margin disciplineDirect-from-manufacturer sourcing holds gross margin as volume grows.

          
05Operational capacityWarehousing, fulfilment and headcount scale ahead of order volume, not behind it.

          
06Market conditionsThe continued migration of regulated safety and consumable categories online.

        

        
£100 million is a target enterprise value, an illustrative future figure based on successful execution of the plan above. It is not a professional valuation and should not be read as one.
